title: Which knot laws are pairwise, and which are gauge copies of the triangular antiferromagnet
claim: A three-place knot has Fourier degree <= 2 iff it excludes one complementary pair (the NAE class); a weave of NAE-class knots with consistent bond signs is a gauge copy of the zero-temperature triangular antiferromagnet (critical) up to torus holonomy; not-exactly-two on the weave is hard hexagons at activity one plus the all-ones state; parity freezes the weave (4 or 1 states).
standard_statement: Fourier degree of 3-bit Boolean functions; Mattis-Toulouse gauge equivalence of frustrated Ising models; hard hexagon model (Baxter); GF(2) linear systems.
prior_work: O'Donnell; Mattis 1976; Toulouse 1977; Fradkin, Huberman and Shenker 1978; Wannier 1950; Stephenson 1964, 1970; Blote and Hilhorst 1982; Nienhuis, Hilhorst and Blote 1984; Baxter 1980; PINNING-20261031-001; DISTANCE-ORDER-20261117-001A.
completion_gate: check.py passes (34 knots; sign test against torus counts; hard hexagon and parity counts), the referee reviews the proofs.

validation.status: check.py run before the freeze; referee pending
validation.independence: independent independent-set transfer for L3; same task authorship
